# Cocos AIR application lifecycle

Use the [environment rules](references/context.md) to locate the checkout or installed package; sibling skills are optional direct dependencies, not a recursive load list.

Build the app handle correctly: admit options before the engine evaluates, run and release scenes through the single per-document runtime, and read context health and session ownership from the handle instead of guessing at engine internals.

## Quick Start

Read [references/quick-start.md](references/quick-start.md) when constructing the minimal example. It preserves the complete setup and teardown sequence; select the source-checkout or npm-consumer environment first.

## Related skills

Read [references/context.md](references/context.md#related-skills) to select the owner of this step and only its directly needed dependencies. Reuse already loaded skills; this is not a recursive load list.

## When to use what

- "Which option values are actually legal, what is the real default, and what does a second `createAirApp` or a restart-after-failure hit?" -> `normalizeAirOptions`, `admitAirOptions` plus `AirAppImpl.close`, [app-options.md](references/app-options.md).
- "`createAirApp` rejected with some `AIR_E_...` / `WEBGL2_REQUIRED`" -> match `error.code`, then [startup-errors.md](references/startup-errors.md).
- "Swap or tear down the running scene without reloading" -> `app.run` / `app.releaseScene!()`, receipt fields in [app-options.md](references/app-options.md).
- "The context was lost; is the app still drawing?" -> `app.contextHealth` / `attachContextHealth`, [context-health.md](references/context-health.md).
- "Register asset, listener and timer cleanup that a scene switch must honour" -> `app.session` / `createSessionScope`, [session-scope.md](references/session-scope.md).
- "Fill the window versus fit a host element, or wire design resolution" -> `screenMode`/`container` and `designResolution` rows in [app-options.md](references/app-options.md); `view.setDesignResolutionSize` is called for you, coordinate-maths routing goes to the camera and UI skills, prose in `docs/manual/design-viewport-and-controls.md`.

## Contracts

One runtime is admitted per document; a closed or failed runtime needs a page reload. Validate options before loading the engine. HEADLESS produces no pixels; context-health observation does not rebuild GPU resources.

Read [references/contracts.md](references/contracts.md) only when the task needs exact option rules, limits, error behavior or source annotations. Prefer the topic references below for a narrower question.

## Common Mistakes

Before implementing the relevant path, read its wrong/right examples in [references/common-mistakes.md](references/common-mistakes.md):

- [HIGH] Importing the engine before the canvas is in the document
- [HIGH] Creating a second app in the same document after close()
- [HIGH] Using renderMode 3 to check rendered pixels
- [MEDIUM] Treating attachContextHealth as automatic device restoration
- [MEDIUM] Resuming in-document to recover from a context loss

## References

- [app-options.md](references/app-options.md) - AirAppOptions table with defaults and enforced ranges, policy and renderMode enum values, startup order and DPR timing, admission and identity rules, container DOM rules, lifecycle method and receipt field tables, declaration inventory and evidence status.
- [startup-errors.md](references/startup-errors.md) - every `AIR_E_*` literal plus `WEBGL2_REQUIRED` and the un-coded import-order errors, with throw site, trigger and remedy.
- [context-health.md](references/context-health.md) - state machine, snapshot and option fields, timeline cap, reload gate, what is not restored.
- [session-scope.md](references/session-scope.md) - generation and token rules, `own()` semantics, dispose timeout maths and receipt statuses.

## Canonical docs

`docs/manual/safe-startup-and-release.md`, `docs/webgl2-only.md`, `docs/manual/design-viewport-and-controls.md`, `docs/manual/scene-switching.md`, `docs/UPSTREAM.md`, `README.md`.

# Cocos AIR glTF contracts

Use the [environment rules](references/context.md) to locate the checkout or installed package; sibling skills are optional direct dependencies, not a recursive load list.

Load glTF and GLB straight from a URL or from bytes, inject your own decoders, instantiate shared assets into independent node trees, and read the support matrix honestly - there is no Creator importer and no bundled Draco, meshopt or KTX2 decoder here.

## Quick Start

Read [references/quick-start.md](references/quick-start.md) when constructing the minimal example. It preserves the complete setup and teardown sequence; select the source-checkout or npm-consumer environment first.

## Related skills

Read [references/context.md](references/context.md#related-skills) to select the owner of this step and only its directly needed dependencies. Reuse already loaded skills; this is not a recursive load list.

## When to use what

- "load a model from a URL" -> `new GLTFLoader().loadAsync(url)`; the asset manager owns caching and in-flight deduplication ([loader-api.md](references/loader-api.md)).
- "load from bytes I already have" -> `parseAsync(data, baseUrl)` with `string | ArrayBuffer`; pass `baseUrl` for a `.gltf` whose buffers and images are relative, and pass nothing for `data:`/`blob:` input (`src/air/assets/gltf/loader.ts:115`, `:200-202`).
- "compressed model" -> inject first, then load; `setMeshoptDecoder`, `setDRACODecoder`, `setKTX2Transcoder` ([decoders.md](references/decoders.md)).
- "does this browser support extension X" -> `getExtensionSupport()`, and read the five statuses rather than assuming ([extensions-matrix.md](references/extensions-matrix.md)).
- "several copies of the same model" -> one `GLTFAsset`, many `instantiate()` calls; meshes, materials, textures and skeletons are shared, node and animation state are not ([loader-api.md](references/loader-api.md)).
- "loop one clip on one instance" -> `instance.setAnimationLoop(true, clipName)`; omit the name to select every clip of that instance.
- "why did my load throw with no code" -> it is a plain `Error`, a `DOMException` or a tagged `TypeError`, not a `GLTFError` ([diagnostics.md](references/diagnostics.md)).
- "write my own extension handler" -> `loader.register(factory)`; registration order is hook execution order, and the context type is not nameable from the declarations ([extensions-matrix.md](references/extensions-matrix.md), [loader-api.md](references/loader-api.md)).

## Contracts

Configure required decoders before loading; declared extension support is not deployed-decoder or browser proof. Dispose instances before shared asset destruction and distinguish GLTFError from tagged TypeError/RangeError.

Read [references/contracts.md](references/contracts.md) only when the task needs exact option rules, limits, error behavior or source annotations. Prefer the topic references below for a narrower question.

## Common Mistakes

Before implementing the relevant path, read its wrong/right examples in [references/common-mistakes.md](references/common-mistakes.md):

- [HIGH] Assuming the decoders are built in
- [HIGH] Reading `decoder-required` as `supported`
- [HIGH] Catching only `GLTFError`
- [MEDIUM] Naming glTF internals that are not on the public face
- [MEDIUM] Expecting `asset.destroy()` to tear down live instances

## References

- [loader-api.md](references/loader-api.md) - the two entry points and import-time registration, loader configuration and option precedence, the ordered `parseAsync` pipeline, the `GLTFAsset` member table and its deferred release, `instantiate(sceneIndex)` visibility versus inclusion and per-scene clip caching, the `GLTFInstance` contract, the public versus internal face, and the per-symbol evidence split.
- [extensions-matrix.md](references/extensions-matrix.md) - the five statuses with their error-code mapping and proof state, how `getExtensionSupport()` computes them, all 21 registrations in hook order with catalog status and official comparison, the required versus optional table, registration-order rules, and what the browser evidence does not cover.
- [decoders.md](references/decoders.md) - why decoders are outside the bundle, the shipped artifact inventory with byte counts, the three setters and three provider factories and their interfaces, the browser module-loading pattern and MIME requirements, the unusable meshopt barrel, the Node-only Draco ruling, the KTX2 ceiling and target formats, and what is actually verified.
- [diagnostics.md](references/diagnostics.md) - the five codes with recomputed throw-site counts, how to discriminate a caught error, the four non-`GLTFError` shapes, the two incompatible report types, where each progress phase is emitted, the warning channel and its one fully silent case, failure containment, and the evidence gap.

## Canonical docs

- `docs/gltf/gltf-runtime.md` - open for the load-and-play walkthrough, the other loading entries, multi-instance resource sharing, the support-boundary table and the material, lighting and instancing semantics behind it.
- `docs/gltf/gltf-extension-reference.md` - open for the general extension contract and the per-family detail: geometry compression, texture encoding, scene extensions and the material extension set, plus the official-sample comparison column.
- `docs/gltf/gltf-decoder-deployment.md` - open for the artifact inventory pointer, the injection API, static serving requirements, nested deployment paths, the offline acceptance gate and the failure-semantics quick reference.
- `build/gltf-decoders/MANIFEST.md` - open for authoritative versions, licenses, per-file byte counts and sha256, the gate identity, and the recorded browser-side Draco decision.

# Cocos AIR materials and effects

Use the [environment rules](references/context.md) to locate the checkout or installed package; sibling skills are optional direct dependencies, not a recursive load list.

A material in AIR is one effect recipe plus a bag of uniform values: `new Material()`, `initialize({ effectName })` picks the recipe, `setProperty(name, value)` fills it. There is no material inheritance tree, no `ShaderMaterial`, and no Editor asset pipeline - recipe names are strings and custom shaders are hand-written compiled effect JSON.

## Quick Start

Read [references/quick-start.md](references/quick-start.md) when constructing the minimal example. It preserves the complete setup and teardown sequence; select the source-checkout or npm-consumer environment first.

## Related skills

Read [references/context.md](references/context.md#related-skills) to select the owner of this step and only its directly needed dependencies. Reuse already loaded skills; this is not a recursive load list.

## When to use what

- "Paint a 3D object, no lighting" -> `initialize({ effectName: 'builtin-unlit' })` + `mainColor`.
- "Physically shaded object" -> `effectName: 'builtin-standard'` + `metallic`/`roughness`/`emissive`; table in [property-types.md](references/property-types.md).
- "Show a texture" -> the map macro FIRST in `initialize({ defines })`, then `setProperty`; `USE_TEXTURE` for unlit and sprite, `USE_ALBEDO_MAP` for standard ([defines.md](references/defines.md)).
- "Two objects, same recipe, different colors" -> two `new Material()`; `Material.copy(src, overrides?)`, never a shared builtin write.
- "Change one renderer without touching its material" -> `renderer.getMaterialInstance(i)` / the `renderer.material` getter; semantics in [builtin-effects.md](references/builtin-effects.md).
- "Change a macro or blend state after initialization" -> `MaterialInstance.recompileShaders` / `MaterialInstance.overridePipelineStates`; a plain `Material` only warns.
- "Write my own GLSL" -> compiled-shape effect JSON + `glsl3` variant + `effect.onLoaded()`; [custom-glsl.md](references/custom-glsl.md).
- "Per-frame uniform" -> cache `pass.getHandle(name)` and call `Pass.setUniform(handle, value)`.
- "Fog on an unlit object" -> `createAirUnlitFogEffect()`.
- "Mask a Sprite" -> `attachAirSpriteMask(sprite, texture, options?)`.
- "What state does this material really have" -> `inspectAirMaterial(material)`, or `inspectAirMeshMaterial(mesh, material)` for define-versus-attribute checks.

## Contracts

Create materials after app/device initialization. Property names and value types must match the effect; `USE_TEXTURE` must match the sampling path. Custom GLSL needs declared layouts and built-in bindings.

Read [references/contracts.md](references/contracts.md) only when the task needs exact option rules, limits, error behavior or source annotations. Prefer the topic references below for a narrower question.

## Common Mistakes

Before implementing the relevant path, read its wrong/right examples in [references/common-mistakes.md](references/common-mistakes.md):

- [HIGH] Setting the texture without its map macro
- [HIGH] Writing a shared material after the renderer instantiated it
- [HIGH] Calling the runtime recompile and state-override API on a plain Material
- [MEDIUM] Hand-writing a glsl3 variant that keeps Vulkan-only members

## References

- [builtin-effects.md](references/builtin-effects.md) - the 21 registered effect entries with definition lines, the 17 builtin material uuids with their `effectName` and `defines`, the registration and `tryCompile` timing, and which names are absent from the bundle export list.
- [property-types.md](references/property-types.md) - `gfx.Type` ordinals, the accepted-JS-value matrix per declared type with its error codes, `Color` byte-versus-fraction conversion, `linear: true` handling, the `setProperty` step order, `handleInfo` alias tables, and the full settable property lists of `builtin-standard` and `builtin-unlit`.
- [custom-glsl.md](references/custom-glsl.md) - effect JSON field contract, variant selection, the four `glsl4 -> glsl3` rules, the `assignEffectBindings` set/binding matrices including `CCSkinning -> 3` and why, registration timing, the `effect-json.mjs` generator and `effect-layout.ts` pre-check, black-screen triage order.
- [defines.md](references/defines.md) - where a macro must appear to have any effect, `USE_TEXTURE` versus `USE_ALBEDO_MAP`, the inert `USE_COLOR` define, the complete declared define lists of unlit, sprite and standard, runtime macro changes, fog defines and `createAirUnlitFogEffect`, define read-back and diagnostics.

## Canonical docs

`docs/manual/materials.md`, `docs/manual/custom-shaders.md`, `docs/manual/uniform-types.md`. Runnable references: `examples/shader-custom-gradient`, `examples/shader-dissolve`, `examples/material-basic`, `examples/material-color`, `examples/material-unlit`, `examples/material-ops`, `examples/material-lifecycle`.

# Cocos AIR project setup

Use the [environment rules](references/context.md) to locate the checkout or installed package; sibling skills are optional direct dependencies, not a recursive load list.

Install, import and type-consume Cocos AIR correctly: one startup path per page, the canvas bound before engine evaluation, the declarations the compiler can resolve, and a build candidate you can name.

## Quick Start

Read [references/quick-start.md](references/quick-start.md) when constructing the minimal example. It preserves the complete setup and teardown sequence; select the source-checkout or npm-consumer environment first.

## Related skills

Read [references/context.md](references/context.md#related-skills) to select the owner of this step and only its directly needed dependencies. Reuse already loaded skills; this is not a recursive load list.

## When to use what

- "Install from npm in a bundler app" -> `cocosair.js` package exports table in [entries.md](references/entries.md).
- "Static page, no bundler" -> importmap and skeleton rules in [html-shell.md](references/html-shell.md).
- "Custom canvas id or options-only DPR" -> the main entry accepts both at createAirApp time, including canvas creation after import. Use an application-owned dynamic main import when deferred loading is useful.
- "Paint live HTML into a `Texture2D`" -> `cocosair.js` (experimental HTML helpers in the main entry) + cocosair-graphics-and-dom.
- "Editor types fail on TypeScript < 5.0" -> `types@<5.0` / `typesVersions` conditions in [entries.md](references/entries.md).
- "Trim or extend what ships" -> `AIR_FEATURES` variant semantics in [feature-flags.md](references/feature-flags.md); a variant is a different candidate, not the default one.
- "Which command wrote this file under build/?" -> artifact ownership table in [entries.md](references/entries.md).

## Contracts

Use `cocosair.js` in bundler apps; `cocosair` is the repository importmap alias. Pass any selected canvas to createAirApp; repeated main calls share startup admission. Keep variant outputs separate from default builds.

Read [references/contracts.md](references/contracts.md) only when the task needs exact option rules, limits, error behavior or source annotations. Prefer the topic references below for a narrower question.

## Common Mistakes

Before implementing the relevant path, read its wrong/right examples in [references/common-mistakes.md](references/common-mistakes.md):

- [HIGH] Importing 'cocosair' from the installed package
- [HIGH] Taking the package surface from src/index.ts
- [MEDIUM] Using removed bootstrap/html-source package subpaths
- [MEDIUM] Treating a variant build as the default candidate

## References

- [entries.md](references/entries.md) - exports map, per-entry symbol surfaces, artifact ownership.
- [feature-flags.md](references/feature-flags.md) - default 26 units, the 7 unselected declared units, AIR_FEATURES/AIR_OUT_DIR semantics.

# Cocos AIR rendering contracts

Use the [environment rules](references/context.md) to locate the checkout or installed package; sibling skills are optional direct dependencies, not a recursive load list.

Configure what the legacy forward pipeline actually draws - light units and the one main light, shadow casting, offscreen camera targets, texture color contracts - and know which pipeline surfaces a Code First app can reach.

## Quick Start

Read [references/quick-start.md](references/quick-start.md) when constructing the minimal example. It preserves the complete setup and teardown sequence; select the source-checkout or npm-consumer environment first.

## Related skills

Read [references/context.md](references/context.md#related-skills) to select the owner of this step and only its directly needed dependencies. Reuse already loaded skills; this is not a recursive load list.

## When to use what

- "Why is the scene the wrong brightness" -> `DirectionalLight.illuminance` (Lux) or `SphereLight`/`PointLight`/`SpotLight` `luminousFlux`/`luminance`; the HDR and LDR slots and every unit constant are in [lighting-units.md](references/lighting-units.md).
- "Which directional light is actually lighting my scene" -> `inspectAirDirectionalLights(scene)` (`src/air/rendering/engine-contracts.ts:104`).
- "Why are there no shadows" -> the support grid in [shadow-matrix.md](references/shadow-matrix.md), then the four switches in Contracts.
- "Can this light type cast at all" -> `PointLight` has no shadow path in the source (`src/cocos/render-scene/scene/point-light.ts:32`); Sphere is never collected by the flow (`src/cocos/rendering/shadow/shadow-flow.ts:122`).
- "Render a mirror, refraction or a second viewpoint into a texture" -> `createAirRenderTarget(options)` (`src/air/rendering/render-target.ts:290`) plus `attachCamera(camera, beforeRender?)` (`:197`); the raw path is `camera.targetTexture`.
- "Feed that texture into a material after a resize" -> `target.bindColor(material, property, passIdx?)` (`:257`), `bindDepth` (`:258`), `readColor(region?)` for pixels (`:262`).
- "Glass or gem refraction from a glTF material" -> `AirTransmissionCapture` (`src/air/rendering/transmission-capture.ts:74`), one per scene, with `TRANSMISSION_LAYER` (`:29`).
- "Is this format plus this decode legal" -> `resolveAirTextureFormat` (`src/air/rendering/color-contract.ts:21`) and `validateAirTextureColorContract` (`:38`).
- "Can I turn bloom on" -> `postProcess` is the only custom-pipeline-side name the default aggregate exports (`src/exports/air.ts:39`); `director.root.usesCustomPipeline` tells you which pipeline is live (`src/cocos/root.ts:121`).

## Contracts

Legacy forward uses one effective main directional light. Check the shadow support matrix and all cast/receive switches. Report requested versus effective MSAA and verify actual pixels.

Read [references/contracts.md](references/contracts.md) only when the task needs exact option rules, limits, error behavior or source annotations. Prefer the topic references below for a narrower question.

## Common Mistakes

Before implementing the relevant path, read its wrong/right examples in [references/common-mistakes.md](references/common-mistakes.md):

- [HIGH] Turning on one shadow switch and expecting a shadow map
- [HIGH] Importing the custom pipeline namespace and expecting post-processing to run
- [HIGH] Adding a second directional light to fill the dark side
- [MEDIUM] Treating a requested sample count as the negotiated one
- [MEDIUM] Letting the color validator stand in for building the texture

## References

- [lighting-units.md](references/lighting-units.md) - light component surface and defaults, `LightType` ordinals, illuminance and luminous-flux ranges with their HDR/LDR slots, `nt2lm`, the exposure and light-meter constants written into the UBO, the `mainLight` limitation text, the full `inspectAirDirectionalLights` return shape, light symbol reachability.

Use the [environment rules](references/context.md) to locate the checkout or installed package; sibling skills are optional direct dependencies, not a recursive load list.

Build Spine, DragonBones, TiledMap, particle and billboard content from strings and bytes at runtime - there is no Creator importer, no uuid dependency graph and no prefab here, and one of these five subsystems cannot run at all in the default bundle.

## Quick Start

## When to use what

| Subsystem     | Runnable today | Import symbols                                                                                  | Constructed from                                   | Main trap                            |
| ------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Spine         | No, BLOCKED    | `sp`, `loadWasmModuleSpine`                                                                     | skeleton json or binary, atlas text, `Texture2D[]` | null runtime data, no error          |
| DragonBones   | Yes            | `dragonBones` namespace                                                                         | two assets from JSON strings plus one `Texture2D`  | asset setters want raw text          |
| TiledMap      | Yes            | `TiledMap`, `TiledMapAsset`, `TiledLayer`, `TiledObjectGroup`, `TiledTile`, `TiledUserNodeData` | tmx XML string, tsx text, sprite frames            | name lookup by parallel arrays       |
| Particle 2D   | Yes            | `ParticleSystem2D`, `ParticleAsset`                                                             | plist text parsed at run time                      | plist key names and blend enum slots |
| Motion streak | Yes            | `MotionStreak`, `MotionStreakAssemblerManager`                                                  | a plain `Texture2D`                                | no `MotionStreak2D` exists           |
| Billboard     | Yes            | `Billboard`                                                                                     | any `Texture2D` the app keeps alive                | `width` and `height` default to 0    |

## Contracts

Create the Canvas component before assigning its camera. Use runtime payloads, not Creator imports. Spine remains backend/asset blocked; particle plist fields and blend factors follow the native runtime contract.

# Cocos AIR agent session and inspection

Use the [environment rules](references/context.md) to locate the checkout or installed package; sibling skills are optional direct dependencies, not a recursive load list.

Drive and observe a running Cocos AIR app through two distinct faces: the runtime face (the `window.__airApp` binding the app sets itself plus the bounded `AirDiagnostics` channel on the main entry) and the devtools face (the `tools/debug/**` session protocol, scene/node snapshots, frame capture, error ring buffer, and pixel probes). The devtools face is NOT part of the default runtime bundle and is not importable from `cocosair`; keep it out of shipped app code.

## Quick Start

Read [references/quick-start.md](references/quick-start.md) when constructing the minimal example. It preserves the complete setup and teardown sequence; select the source-checkout or npm-consumer environment first.

## Related skills

Read [references/context.md](references/context.md#related-skills) to select the owner of this step and only its directly needed dependencies. Reuse already loaded skills; this is not a recursive load list.

## When to use what

- "let an agent or panel see the running app" -> the app sets `window.__airApp = app` (`examples/automation/main.ts:31`); the devtools panel reads `options.app ?? window.__airApp` (`tools/debug/panel.ts:67`). There is no runtime global the engine installs for you.
- "read the scene structure" -> `session.inspectScene()` for a flat `SceneSummary`, `session.inspectNode(id)` for a `NodeSummary` (`tools/debug/agent-session.ts:451`, `:505`). Observation is read-only and never adds asset refs.
- "apply a controlled change" -> `session.dispatch({ requestId, action, targetId, params })` for a whitelisted write (`tools/debug/agent-session.ts:665`). Writes require the target to be inside `writableScenes`; otherwise `OUT_OF_SCOPE`.
- "prove a frame changed" -> `session.captureFrame()` reads the canvas on the AFTER_DRAW hook (`tools/debug/agent-session.ts:589`).
- "collect what broke at runtime" -> devtools `session.getRuntimeErrors()` ring buffer (`tools/debug/agent-session.ts:647`) versus the runtime `app.diagnostics` bounded channel (`src/air/diagnostics.ts:14`).
- "measure a rendered region" -> `tools/debug/pixel-regions.mjs` conventions, screenshot top-left origin versus raw canvas bottom-left (`tools/debug/pixel-regions.mjs:5`, `:53`).

## Contracts

Agent sessions are devtools-only and require explicit writable scope. Inspect session-local IDs before writes. Duplicate request IDs are rejected; capture waits for AFTER_DRAW. Runtime diagnostics are a separate API.

Read [references/contracts.md](references/contracts.md) only when the task needs exact option rules, limits, error behavior or source annotations. Prefer the topic references below for a narrower question.

## Common Mistakes

Before implementing the relevant path, read its wrong/right examples in [references/common-mistakes.md](references/common-mistakes.md):

- [HIGH] Blindly retrying a write with the same requestId
- [HIGH] Treating the devtools session as a default-runtime API in app code
- [MEDIUM] Confusing the runtime diagnostics channel with the devtools error ring buffer
- [MEDIUM] Reading raw canvas pixels with a screenshot-style origin

- [runtime-control.md](references/runtime-control.md) - the `window.__airApp` binding, scene/node snapshot shapes, ID stability, STALE_TARGET semantics and the runtime AirDiagnostics bounded channel versus the devtools error ring buffer.

# Cocos AIR animation and tween contracts

Use the [environment rules](references/context.md) to locate the checkout or installed package; sibling skills are optional direct dependencies, not a recursive load list.

Move things over time two ways: the code-first `tween(target)` chain (zero assets, the shortest path) and the native `Animation` component driving an `AnimationClip` you can build entirely in code. Both are stepped by the director, never by your own `requestAnimationFrame`. For deterministic evidence there is a third, test-only driver, `createStepClock`, that pauses the real clock and advances one frame at a time.

## Quick Start

Read [references/quick-start.md](references/quick-start.md) when constructing the minimal example. It preserves the complete setup and teardown sequence; select the source-checkout or npm-consumer environment first.

## Related skills

Read [references/context.md](references/context.md#related-skills) to select the owner of this step and only its directly needed dependencies. Reuse already loaded skills; this is not a recursive load list.

## When to use what

- "move/scale/rotate something over time, no assets" -> `tween(target).to(...).start()`; the chain is a sequence and `repeatForever()` loops the union ([tween-ops.md](references/tween-ops.md)).
- "run two motions at once on one target" -> just start two tweens on the same target; they time independently. `parallel(...)` is only for packing a parallel group into a larger sequence.
- "reusable keyed animation, or a glTF clip" -> `Animation` component + `AnimationClip`; build the clip in code with `animation.VectorTrack` and `animation.TrackPath` ([animation-clip.md](references/animation-clip.md)).
- "loop a clip" -> set `clip.wrapMode = AnimationClip.WrapMode.Loop` before play, or set `state.wrapMode` (which resets time and repeatCount) ([animation-clip.md](references/animation-clip.md)).
- "per-frame game logic" -> `Component.update(dt)` / `lateUpdate(dt)` / `this.schedule(cb, interval)`; multiply by `dt`, never assume a fixed frame rate (`docs/manual/how-to-update-things.md`).
- "deterministic frames for a test or evidence capture" -> `createStepClock()`; `begin()` then `await step(dt)` then `end()`, and never run it while the real pacer is live ([step-clock.md](references/step-clock.md)).
- "state-machine / pose-graph animation" -> not published; `marionette` and `procedural-animation` are out of the default feature set ([animation-clip.md](references/animation-clip.md)).

## Contracts

Use one clock for native updates and deterministic steps. Preserve tween target ownership; pose-graph availability requires checking the actual entry. `WrapMode` is accessed through `AnimationClip.WrapMode`.

Read [references/contracts.md](references/contracts.md) only when the task needs exact option rules, limits, error behavior or source annotations. Prefer the topic references below for a narrower question.

## Common Mistakes

Before implementing the relevant path, read its wrong/right examples in [references/common-mistakes.md](references/common-mistakes.md):

- [HIGH] Importing track classes by name
- [HIGH] Running the real pacer and the step clock at once
- [HIGH] Assuming `reverseTime(embedTween)` returns to the start
- [MEDIUM] Setting `wrapMode` every frame to keep a clip looping
- [MEDIUM] Citing marionette or pose-graph animation as available

## References

- [animation-clip.md](references/animation-clip.md) - the `Animation` component surface and lifecycle, `AnimationState` and the wrapMode setter reset, `AnimationClip` construction and members, the `WrapMode` bitmask enum, the `animation` namespace and `TrackPath` builders, and the marionette/pose-graph exclusion with its build-time switches.
- [tween-ops.md](references/tween-ops.md) - the full `Tween` chain (to/by/set/delay/call/update/sequence/parallel/repeat/repeatForever/reverseTime/union/clone/timeScale), lifecycle (start/stop/pause/resume/running), the target-bound statics, node-state binding, `TweenSystem` and the ActionManager, and the GAP-T1 reverseTime defect.

# Cocos AIR camera

Use the [environment rules](references/context.md) to locate the checkout or installed package; sibling skills are optional direct dependencies, not a recursive load list.

Frame a scene with the original `Camera` component: choose the projection and its clip planes, decide which layers it draws and in what order, and convert between world space and the physical screen rectangle it renders into. AIR ships no Creator camera preview; every camera is built and configured in code.

## Quick Start

Read [references/quick-start.md](references/quick-start.md) when constructing the minimal example. It preserves the complete setup and teardown sequence; select the source-checkout or npm-consumer environment first.

## When to use what

- "Put a view into a scene" -> `node.addComponent(Camera)`; the render object is `camera.camera` (`src/cocos/misc/camera-component.ts:202`).
- "Switch perspective and orthographic framing" -> `camera.projection`, plus `fov`/`fovAxis` or `orthoHeight`/`orthoWidth`; table in [camera-projection.md](references/camera-projection.md).
- "Fit a loaded model in view" -> `frameObject(camera, target, fallbackDistance?)` (`src/air/utils/frame-object.ts:35`).
- "Split-screen or picture-in-picture" -> `camera.rect` (normalized viewport `Rect`).
- "Two cameras, who draws on top" -> `camera.priority` + `camera.clearFlags`; behavior in [multi-camera.md](references/multi-camera.md).
- "Which nodes does this camera draw" -> `camera.visibility` layer mask (bit values owned by cocosair-scene-graph).
- "Convert a pointer pixel to a world ray / node position" -> `camera.screenToWorld`, `camera.screenPointToRay`, `camera.convertToUINode`; coordinate space in [screen-world.md](references/screen-world.md).
- "Clip at an arbitrary near plane (mirror, water)" -> `camera.camera.calculateObliqueMat(Vec4)` and `camera.camera.getClipSpaceMinz()`.

## Contracts

Use component conversion methods and left-bottom framebuffer pixels. `worldToScreen` and `screenToWorld` use different depth conventions; prefer a ray for picking. Camera visibility must include the node layer.

# Cocos AIR glTF contracts

Use the [environment rules](references/context.md) to locate the checkout or installed package; sibling skills are optional direct dependencies, not a recursive load list.

Load glTF and GLB straight from a URL or from bytes, inject your own decoders, instantiate shared assets into independent node trees, and read the support matrix honestly - there is no Creator importer and no bundled Draco, meshopt or KTX2 decoder here.

## Quick Start

Read [references/quick-start.md](references/quick-start.md) when constructing the minimal example. It preserves the complete setup and teardown sequence; select the source-checkout or npm-consumer environment first.

## Related skills

Read [references/context.md](references/context.md#related-skills) to select the owner of this step and only its directly needed dependencies. Reuse already loaded skills; this is not a recursive load list.

## When to use what

- "load a model from a URL" -> `new GLTFLoader().loadAsync(url)`; the asset manager owns caching and in-flight deduplication ([loader-api.md](references/loader-api.md)).
- "load from bytes I already have" -> `parseAsync(data, baseUrl)` with `string | ArrayBuffer`; pass `baseUrl` for a `.gltf` whose buffers and images are relative, and pass nothing for `data:`/`blob:` input (`src/air/assets/gltf/loader.ts:115`, `:200-202`).
- "compressed model" -> inject first, then load; `setMeshoptDecoder`, `setDRACODecoder`, `setKTX2Transcoder` ([decoders.md](references/decoders.md)).
- "does this browser support extension X" -> `getExtensionSupport()`, and read the five statuses rather than assuming ([extensions-matrix.md](references/extensions-matrix.md)).
- "several copies of the same model" -> one `GLTFAsset`, many `instantiate()` calls; meshes, materials, textures and skeletons are shared, node and animation state are not ([loader-api.md](references/loader-api.md)).
- "loop one clip on one instance" -> `instance.setAnimationLoop(true, clipName)`; omit the name to select every clip of that instance.
- "why did my load throw with no code" -> it is a plain `Error`, a `DOMException` or a tagged `TypeError`, not a `GLTFError` ([diagnostics.md](references/diagnostics.md)).
- "write my own extension handler" -> `loader.register(factory)`; registration order is hook execution order, and the context type is not nameable from the declarations ([extensions-matrix.md](references/extensions-matrix.md), [loader-api.md](references/loader-api.md)).

## Contracts

Configure required decoders before loading; declared extension support is not deployed-decoder or browser proof. Dispose instances before shared asset destruction and distinguish GLTFError from tagged TypeError/RangeError.

texture or a DOM element, and opt into the experimental HTML canvas texture. The

## When to use what

- "draw a shape in code" -> build `AirGraphicsCommand[]`, replay solid fills with `drawAirGraphics` on a `Graphics` component (`src/air/graphics-commands.ts:74-88`).
- "export vector art" -> `airGraphicsCommandsToSvg(commands, bounds)`; it keeps the original curves, the `Graphics` mesh does not (`src/air/graphics-commands.ts:92-157`).
- "gradient, radial, pattern or evenodd hole" -> `rasterizeAirGraphics(commands, options)` for a Canvas2D `Texture2D`, then display it (`src/air/graphics-raster.ts:11-85`).
- "show a texture in UI" -> `createAirTextureSprite(parent, texture, options)`; the texture stays borrowed (`src/air/texture-sprite.ts:15-48`).
- "cut one Sprite by another texture" -> `attachAirSpriteMask(sprite, maskTexture, options)` (`src/air/effects/sprite-mask.ts:18-83`).
- "make a subtree add/multiply" -> `createAirUIBlendScope(root, mode)` (`src/air/ui-blend.ts:11-55`).
- "keep a DOM input glued to a UI node" -> `createAirDOMOverlay({ canvas })` then `.attach(...)` (`src/air/dom-overlay.ts:24-83`).
- "warp a textured UI quad by hand" -> add the `AirUIMesh` component and `setGeometry(...)` (`src/air/ui-mesh.ts:83-118`).
- "paint a live form as a GPU texture" -> the experimental HTML helpers exported by `cocosair.js` (see [html-source.md](references/html-source.md)).

## Contracts

Use native Graphics for solid nonzero fills and rasterization for rich fills. Texture/element bindings borrow their sources and need explicit updates and disposal. Live HTML textures require the experimental subpath.

# Cocos AIR native input and the action layer

Use the [environment rules](references/context.md) to locate the checkout or installed package; sibling skills are optional direct dependencies, not a recursive load list.

Read real events through `input` / `systemEvent`, then drive gameplay through the AIR action layer: `createActionState` holds the state machine, `createActionInput` wires one backend to it, `createSessionGate` admits or rejects, and `SceneStack` navigates persistent pages.

## Quick Start

Read [references/quick-start.md](references/quick-start.md) when constructing the minimal example. It preserves the complete setup and teardown sequence; select the source-checkout or npm-consumer environment first.

## Related skills

Read [references/context.md](references/context.md#related-skills) to select the owner of this step and only its directly needed dependencies. Reuse already loaded skills; this is not a recursive load list.

## When to use what

- "React to a touch, key or mouse directly" -> `input.on(Input.EventType.X, handler)` for the unified feed and `systemEvent.on(SystemEvent.EventType.X, handler)` for the raw feed (`src/cocos/input/input.ts:160`, `src/cocos/input/system-event.ts:72`); the event classes are `EventTouch`/`EventKeyboard`/`EventMouse`, keys come from `KeyCode`.
- "Map held keys/pointers to named game actions" -> `createActionState` (pure reducer) plus `createActionInput` (one backend); query with `held`/`pressed`/`released`/`axis` and drain edges with `consumeTick` (`src/air/action-state.ts:124-172`).
- "Gate a paused or backgrounded app" -> `createSessionGate` and its `active`/`generation`; pass it as the adapter's `session` (`src/air/action-input.ts:69-100`).
- "Persistent-page push/pop with preserved state" -> `SceneStack` over one long-lived `Scene` (`src/air/scene-stack.ts:47-188`); use `app.run()` replacement instead for a full scene swap (owned by the application skill).

## Contracts

Keep native and DOM action-source contracts distinct; DOM input needs an explicit canvas. Pair each listener with its own callback-specific off. Respect session generations, focus and SceneStack input blocking.

- [HIGH] Using the dom backend and expecting the canvas to be found for you
- [HIGH] Assuming reset() unhooked the event listeners

# Cocos AIR materials and effects

Use the [environment rules](references/context.md) to locate the checkout or installed package; sibling skills are optional direct dependencies, not a recursive load list.

A material in AIR is one effect recipe plus a bag of uniform values: `new Material()`, `initialize({ effectName })` picks the recipe, `setProperty(name, value)` fills it. There is no material inheritance tree, no `ShaderMaterial`, and no Editor asset pipeline - recipe names are strings and custom shaders are hand-written compiled effect JSON.

## Quick Start

Read [references/quick-start.md](references/quick-start.md) when constructing the minimal example. It preserves the complete setup and teardown sequence; select the source-checkout or npm-consumer environment first.

## Related skills

Read [references/context.md](references/context.md#related-skills) to select the owner of this step and only its directly needed dependencies. Reuse already loaded skills; this is not a recursive load list.

## When to use what

- "Paint a 3D object, no lighting" -> `initialize({ effectName: 'builtin-unlit' })` + `mainColor`.
- "Physically shaded object" -> `effectName: 'builtin-standard'` + `metallic`/`roughness`/`emissive`; table in [property-types.md](references/property-types.md).
- "Show a texture" -> the map macro FIRST in `initialize({ defines })`, then `setProperty`; `USE_TEXTURE` for unlit and sprite, `USE_ALBEDO_MAP` for standard ([defines.md](references/defines.md)).
- "Two objects, same recipe, different colors" -> two `new Material()`; `Material.copy(src, overrides?)`, never a shared builtin write.
- "Change one renderer without touching its material" -> `renderer.getMaterialInstance(i)` / the `renderer.material` getter; semantics in [builtin-effects.md](references/builtin-effects.md).
- "Change a macro or blend state after initialization" -> `MaterialInstance.recompileShaders` / `MaterialInstance.overridePipelineStates`; a plain `Material` only warns.
- "Write my own GLSL" -> compiled-shape effect JSON + `glsl3` variant + `effect.onLoaded()`; [custom-glsl.md](references/custom-glsl.md).
- "Per-frame uniform" -> cache `pass.getHandle(name)` and call `Pass.setUniform(handle, value)`.
- "Fog on an unlit object" -> `createAirUnlitFogEffect()`.
- "Mask a Sprite" -> `attachAirSpriteMask(sprite, texture, options?)`.
- "What state does this material really have" -> `inspectAirMaterial(material)`, or `inspectAirMeshMaterial(mesh, material)` for define-versus-attribute checks.

## Contracts

Create materials after app/device initialization. Property names and value types must match the effect; `USE_TEXTURE` must match the sampling path. Custom GLSL needs declared layouts and built-in bindings.

Read [references/contracts.md](references/contracts.md) only when the task needs exact option rules, limits, error behavior or source annotations. Prefer the topic references below for a narrower question.

## Common Mistakes

Before implementing the relevant path, read its wrong/right examples in [references/common-mistakes.md](references/common-mistakes.md):

- [HIGH] Setting the texture without its map macro
- [HIGH] Writing a shared material after the renderer instantiated it
- [HIGH] Calling the runtime recompile and state-override API on a plain Material
- [MEDIUM] Hand-writing a glsl3 variant that keeps Vulkan-only members

# Cocos AIR math

Use the [environment rules](references/context.md) to locate the checkout or installed package; sibling skills are optional direct dependencies, not a recursive load list.

Compute with the value types the scene graph itself consumes: mutable instance fields, static operations that write into their first `out` argument, and matrices the `Node` transform pipeline reads back.

## Quick Start

Read [references/quick-start.md](references/quick-start.md) when constructing the minimal example. It preserves the complete setup and teardown sequence; select the source-checkout or npm-consumer environment first.

## Related skills

Read [references/context.md](references/context.md#related-skills) to select the owner of this step and only its directly needed dependencies. Reuse already loaded skills; this is not a recursive load list.

## When to use what

- "Normalize / length / dot / cross a direction" -> `Vec3.normalize`, `Vec3.len`, `Vec3.dot`, `Vec3.cross` (`src/cocos/core/math/vec3.ts:329`, `:360`); table in [value-types.md](references/value-types.md).
- "Angle between two vectors" -> `Vec3.angle(a, b)` RADIANS (`src/cocos/core/math/vec3.ts:753`), `Vec2.angle` (`src/cocos/core/math/vec2.ts:438`); the signed form is `Vec3.signedAngle` (`src/cocos/core/math/vec3.ts:791`, table in [value-types.md](references/value-types.md)) and there is no `Vec2.signedAngle`.
- "Build a transform matrix / read TRS back out" -> `Mat4.fromSRT(out, q, v, s)` (`src/cocos/core/math/mat4.ts:964`) and `Mat4.toSRT(m, q, v, s)` (`:878`); there is no `Mat4.decompose`. Element layout in [transforms.md](references/transforms.md).
- "Rotate a quaternion" -> `Quat.fromEuler` degrees YZX (`src/cocos/core/math/quat.ts:557`), `Quat.fromAxisAngle` radians (`:475`), `Quat.rotationTo` (`:104`).
- "Point / rect hit test" -> `Rect.contains(point: Vec2)` (`src/cocos/core/math/rect.ts:414`), `Rect.intersects` (`:399`), `Rect.fromMinMax` (`:56`).
- "Color from a design token string" -> `new Color('#ff8000')`, `Color.fromHEX` (`src/cocos/core/math/color.ts:150`), `toCSS`/`toHEX` (`:497`, `:561`).
- "Interpolate a scalar over time" -> `lerp`/`inverseLerp`/`clamp01`/`repeat`/`pingPong` (`src/cocos/core/math/utils.ts:157`, `:307`, `:146`, `:279`, `:293`).
- "Pick an easing curve" -> `easing.cubicOut` and the rest of the 44 functions (`src/cocos/core/algorithm/easing.ts`, inventory in [easing-random.md](references/easing-random.md)).
- "Deterministic random" -> `pseudoRandom(seed)` (`src/cocos/core/math/utils.ts:227`); "non-reproducible" -> `random`/`randomRange` (`:182`, `:203`).
- "Texture-size rounding / bit math / pack a scalar to 16-bit" -> `bits.nextPow2`, `bits.log2`, `bits.isPow2` (`src/cocos/core/math/bits.ts:151`, `:101`, `:93`) and `floatToHalf`/`halfToFloat` (`src/cocos/core/math/utils.ts:417`, `:421`).

## Contracts

Static math operations use the out-first convention; avoid mutating frozen constants. Matrices are column-major and child world transforms compose parent world with child local.

# Cocos AIR performance contracts

Use the [environment rules](references/context.md) to locate the checkout or installed package; sibling skills are optional direct dependencies, not a recursive load list.

Cut draw calls through the three documented batching routes and the one instancing macro, keep 2D sprites batchable, and read the frame budget with the profiler singleton plus pause/step rendering.

## Quick Start

Read [references/quick-start.md](references/quick-start.md) when constructing the minimal example. It preserves the complete setup and teardown sequence; select the source-checkout or npm-consumer environment first.

## Related skills

Read [references/context.md](references/context.md#related-skills) to select the owner of this step and only its directly needed dependencies. Reuse already loaded skills; this is not a recursive load list.

## When to use what

- "1000 identical cubes and I get 1000 draws" -> route 1 stays 1000 unless the shared material carries `defines: { USE_INSTANCING: true }`, then `Math.ceil(1000 / 1024)` = 1 draw ([instancing.md](references/instancing.md)).
- "those cubes never move again" -> `BatchingUtility.batchStaticModel(grid, batchedRoot)` (`src/cocos/3d/misc/batch-utils.ts:65`), 1 draw at 256 and at 50000 quads (`docs/manual/batching-recipes.md:61-62`).
- "the cube count or the vertex data changes every frame" -> `utils.MeshUtils.createDynamicMesh` (`src/cocos/3d/misc/create-mesh.ts:419`) plus `Mesh.updateSubMesh` (`src/cocos/3d/assets/mesh.ts:588`).
- "two meshes refuse to merge" -> `Mesh.validateMergingMesh` (`src/cocos/3d/assets/mesh.ts:1085`) compares bundle count, attribute formats, primitive count and mode, and rejects a dynamic mesh before `Mesh.merge` (`:771`) returns `false`.
- "how many draws did that actually save" -> `profiler.showStats()` and its `draws` row (`src/cocos/profiler/profiler.ts:590`); the harness asserts against the live counter instead of trusting the route name (`examples/shared/batching-routes.ts:179-180`).
- "do I need a static-batch component for UI" -> no: `UIStaticBatch` is inert in this fork (`src/cocos/2d/components/ui-static-batch.ts:85`, `:106`), and auto-batching keys are in [batching-routes.md](references/batching-routes.md).
- "UI sprites with many different textures" -> the dynamic atlas acceptance rules and knob defaults in [dynamic-atlas.md](references/dynamic-atlas.md).
- "my sprites stopped batching after I repainted a texture" -> texture hash is part of the batch key (`src/cocos/2d/renderer/render-data.ts:460-463`), so a new texture object starts a new batch even for identical pixels.
- "is my loop actually paused" -> `game.isPaused()` (`src/cocos/game/game.ts:615`); `director.isPaused()` (`src/cocos/game/director.ts:693`) reports only the logic gate and stays false while the main loop is stopped.
- "the device is too slow at DPR 3" -> `pixelRatioCap` in the app options (`src/air/app.ts:81`), then `resolutionScale` only when you accept softer text.
- "can I trust the 50k starfield number as a budget" -> no, the recorded evidence covers visibility, interaction and release only ([profiles.md](references/profiles.md)).

## Contracts

Choose static merge, dynamic atlas or instancing according to the scene and material. Measure actual draw counts. For on-demand rendering, wait for the first draw before pausing and keep one step clock.

Read [references/contracts.md](references/contracts.md) only when the task needs exact option rules, limits, error behavior or source annotations. Prefer the topic references below for a narrower question.

## When to use what

## When to use what

- "put UI on screen" -> `createUICanvas(scene, name, { designWidth, designHeight, layer })`; it wires Canvas + Widget + ortho camera in one call (`src/air/ui-kit.ts:37-67`).
- "a colored panel / image" -> `spriteNode(parent, name, { size, position, color, layer })`, then assign `sprite.spriteFrame`; set `SizeMode.CUSTOM` before the frame (`src/air/ui-kit.ts:81-93`, `docs/manual/2d-ui.md:62-66`).
- "on-screen text" -> `labelNode(parent, text, name, { fontSize, position, color, overflow, enableWrapText, boxSize })`; system font unless you bind a BMFont (`src/air/ui-kit.ts:111-131`).
- "align to an edge / fill the screen" -> `Widget` with `isAlignLeft/Right/Top/Bottom` and `alignMode` (`src/cocos/ui/widget.ts:123-148`).
- "auto-stack or grid children" -> `Layout` (`Layout.Type`, `Layout.ResizeMode`, `Layout.VerticalDirection`) (`src/cocos/ui/layout.ts:214`, `:619-644`).

- "wrong 2D overlap" -> `Sorting2D` (needs a `UIRenderer`) writes `uiRenderer.priority` from `SortingLayers` ([sorting.md](references/sorting.md)).

## Contracts

UI renderers need a Canvas, its orthographic camera and matching UI layer/visibility. Use `createUICanvas` to assemble this host. Label uses system fonts unless a supported single-page bitmap font is explicitly bound.

# AIR verification gates and evidence

Use the [environment rules](references/context.md) to locate the checkout or installed package; sibling skills are optional direct dependencies, not a recursive load list.

Verification in this repository separates three claims that an agent tends to collapse into one: that a symbol is exported from source, that it is reachable in the built default bundle, and that it behaves correctly in a real browser. Each npm gate proves one layer, and passing a lower layer does not prove the next. Read the command's documented write behavior before running it, because several gates named `verify:*` rewrite repository content.

## Quick Start

Read [references/quick-start.md](references/quick-start.md) when constructing the minimal example. It preserves the complete setup and teardown sequence; select the source-checkout or npm-consumer environment first.

## Related skills

Read [references/context.md](references/context.md#related-skills) to select the owner of this step and only its directly needed dependencies. Reuse already loaded skills; this is not a recursive load list.

## When to use what

- "did my source change break a contract" -> `npm run typecheck`, then `npm run verify:web-only` for the Web-only dependency boundary, then `npm test -- --runInBand` for logic and resource ownership (HEADLESS, so no pixel claims).
- "is a name reachable in the shipped default bundle" -> inspect its actual export and validate the import/bundler resolution for that entry and candidate. `verify:feature-exports` and `verify:custom-exports` are scoped structural checks, not general export-resolution proof; see [report-layers.md](references/report-layers.md).
- "will an npm consumer actually import it" -> `node tools/verify/graphics-package.cjs --out=<scratch.json>` or `npm run verify:consumer`; they pack and install offline and check real resolution and declaration consumption.
- "does it render correctly in a browser" -> the browser evidence collectors listed in [gate-catalog.md](references/gate-catalog.md); each needs Playwright tooling and matching browser binaries.
- "am I ready to release" -> `npm run verify:release`, and only after the relevant builds and evidence are current; it demands a clean worktree and aggregates existing evidence rather than recapturing it.
- "I need to know what a command does" -> read AGENTS.md's per-command table and [gate-catalog.md](references/gate-catalog.md); do not run a write gate to discover it.

## Contracts

Run repository gates only in a source checkout. Coverage requires matching spec/source/candidate fingerprints and per-API proof. A subset, HEADLESS pass or GPU readback alone cannot establish full browser or release acceptance.

Read [references/contracts.md](references/contracts.md) only when the task needs exact option rules, limits, error behavior or source annotations. Prefer the topic references below for a narrower question.

## Common Mistakes

Before implementing the relevant path, read its wrong/right examples in [references/common-mistakes.md](references/common-mistakes.md):

- [HIGH] Calling a change release-ready from a subset PASS
- [HIGH] Treating an older round's evidence as current
- [HIGH] Running a write gate just to learn what it does
- [MEDIUM] Reading a green import, a HEADLESS pass, or a readback as browser proof

# Cocos AIR skill router

Choose one primary subsystem for the requested outcome, then load only direct dependencies needed by that task. Reuse this router once loaded; related-skill lists are optional routes, not instructions to load the whole suite. Resolve the working environment before reading source paths or running commands.

## Quick Start

```ts
import { createAirApp, Scene } from 'cocosair.js';

const app = await createAirApp({ canvas: '#GameCanvas' });
app.run(new Scene('Main'));
app.getScene(); // -> Scene | null
```

Use the single `cocosair.js` browser entry. Main may be imported before creating the canvas; pass the selected element and pixelRatioCap to createAirApp. No pre-import canvas/DPR global assignment is required. For lazy loading use an application-owned dynamic main import; bootstrap/html-source are no longer public subpaths.

## Related skills

Read [references/context.md](references/context.md#related-skills) to select the owner of this step and only its directly needed dependencies. Reuse already loaded skills; this is not a recursive load list.

## Routing across boundaries

- Startup errors -> application; unresolved imports or package entries -> project-setup.
- Load and animate a glTF model -> gltf primary; add skinning-morph or animation-tween only for the relevant deformation/playback issue.
- Load a bitmap font -> assets; bind an existing font to Label -> ui-2d.
- Debug DOM overlay clicks -> graphics-and-dom; add input-action only when focus/action routing is implicated.
- Implement a visual feature -> its subsystem primary; consult verification for the relevant collector or evidence question, not as a mandatory full gate sequence.

For a broad application, choose the primary skill for the current step and change it as the next concrete step changes. For an unmatched request, inspect the relevant installed declarations/manual chapter; use skill-index search terms to locate an owner. Ask for clarification only when the missing environment or intended behavior affects the result.

## When to use what

- "Why did startup throw `WEBGL2_REQUIRED`?" -> the context has no usable WebGL 2; there is no fallback (Contracts).
- "Which class holds my data?" -> original `Node`/`Component`; view via `Camera`; pixels via `Material` + `Texture2D` and renderers (`Sprite`, `SkinnedMeshRenderer`).
- "Is this capability usable?" -> answer with the three-layer vocabulary below, never "the docs mention it".

## Code First discipline

Read the relevant README/manual chapter from the located package or checkout. Source-only provenance is not an npm dependency; see [environment.md](references/environment.md).

1. Original APIs first: use the engine's `Scene`, `Node`, `Camera`, `Component`, `Material`, `Texture2D` and `Sprite`; AIR helpers compose these objects. Do not invent parallel scene, node or material abstractions.
2. Browser rendering requires WebGL 2 and nothing else; unsupported contexts reject startup with `WEBGL2_REQUIRED`. WebGL 1, Canvas and WebGPU are not supported renderer fallbacks. HEADLESS tests produce no rendered pixels.
3. Use only the browser main entry `cocosair.js`. Main import before canvas creation is supported; pass canvas and pixelRatioCap to createAirApp. For deferred loading, dynamically import the main entry in the application. Startup and HTML texture helpers share the main declarations; there are no bootstrap/html-source package subpaths.
4. Native material property writes require declared properties and matching value types; `USE_TEXTURE` must match whether the effect samples a texture.
5. Keep ownership explicit. Detach renderers and bindings before destroying their textures; borrow shared assets and release only resources the feature owns.
6. Skeletal joints use full paths relative to the skinning root. For glTF decoders and Spine, inspect their documented deployment and license boundaries.

For DOM overlays, SVG, rich fills and sprite masks, read `docs/manual/graphics-and-dom.md` and load cocosair-graphics-and-dom. HTML texture APIs are experimental and live in the opt-in `cocosair.js` entry; ordinary DOM overlays remain a separate capability.

## Contracts

- Capability layers, never conflated: source export (symbol present in that entry's `.d.ts`) / default-bundle reachable (exported and wired through the default aggregate entry; feature-set membership alone is not reachability - the `custom-pipeline-post-process` feature is in the default feature list at `tools/build/build.cjs:43`, yet post-process is unreachable in AIR's current shipping posture and is resolved as variant-build evidence only, `docs/reference/owner-decisions.md:42` row 6 / D11 / LV12-17) / browser-verified (executed PASS against the current candidate with evidence). "Mentioned in docs" is none of the three. `docs/manual/runtime-capability-layers.md` is the reference and splits further into exported / bundled / configured / verified; a default build and an `AIR_FEATURES` variant are different candidates.
- Validate changed behavior in a real browser. A typecheck or the existence of source/API declarations does not prove rendering, interaction or lifecycle behavior.

## Common Mistakes

### [HIGH] Importing the main entry before the canvas exists

Wrong:

```html
<script type="module">
  const { createAirApp } = await import('cocosair.js'); // #GameCanvas not in DOM yet
</script>
```

Correct:

```html
<canvas id="GameCanvas"></canvas>
<script type="module">
  import { createAirApp } from 'cocosair.js';
  const app = await createAirApp({ canvas: '#GameCanvas' });
  const cc = await import('cocosair.js');
</script>
```

Pages adapted from Creator or other engines add the canvas from script; the screen adapter initializes during main-entry import, so startup fails before any app code runs.

### [HIGH] Assuming the Creator asset pipeline exists

Wrong:

```ts
assetManager.loadAny({ bundle: 'resources', path: 'models/robot' });
```

Correct:

```ts
import { Scene, Node } from 'cocosair.js';
// Build the scene in code with the original classes - there is no resources bundle to load from.
const scene = new Scene('Main');
scene.addChild(new Node('Robot')); // Scene extends Node: attach children to it directly
// Load models through the documented glTF path; route every other asset through cocosair-assets.
```

AIR ships no Creator Editor or `.scene`/Prefab/`resources` bundle pipeline; a Creator-parity load fails on the missing bundle instead of falling back.

### [MEDIUM] Treating a docs mention as a usable capability

Wrong:

```ts
// "the repo has pose-graph notes, so I can ship pose-graph animation" - assume reachability from a mention.
import { MarionetteController } from 'cocosair.js'; // absent from the default entry: marionette is not in the default feature set
```

Correct:

```ts
// Answer from a layer you state yourself - this is not an engine export:
type CapabilityLayer = 'source-export' | 'bundle-reachable' | 'browser-verified';
// Then cite that entry's .d.ts and current evidence; the pose graph is neither.
```

Docs enumerate the engine surface; bundle reachability and browser verification are separate candidates, and conflating them produces demos that cannot run.

## No route matched

Read the current main-entry declarations and `docs/manual/index.md` from the located package or checkout. Startup and HTML APIs use the same main-entry declarations. Missing source or sibling skills are environment limitations; use available canonical docs without inventing APIs or a repository root.

When adding, moving or editing suite references, run `node skills/cocosair/scripts/check-paths.cjs` from the checkout or package root. It checks local Markdown targets and rejects unlinked navigation paths in prose; it does not check source provenance, external URLs, anchors or runtime behavior. Use the [environment rules](references/context.md) to locate the checkout or installed package; sibling skills are optional direct dependencies, not a recursive load list.

Build Spine, DragonBones, TiledMap, particle and billboard content from strings and bytes at runtime - there is no Creator importer, no uuid dependency graph and no prefab here, and one of these five subsystems cannot run at all in the default bundle.

## Quick Start

Read [references/quick-start.md](references/quick-start.md) when constructing the minimal example. It preserves the complete setup and teardown sequence; select the source-checkout or npm-consumer environment first.

## Related skills

## When to use what

| Subsystem     | Runnable today | Import symbols                                                                                  | Constructed from                                   | Main trap                            |
| ------------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Spine         | No, BLOCKED    | `sp`, `loadWasmModuleSpine`                                                                     | skeleton json or binary, atlas text, `Texture2D[]` | null runtime data, no error          |
| DragonBones   | Yes            | `dragonBones` namespace                                                                         | two assets from JSON strings plus one `Texture2D`  | asset setters want raw text          |
| TiledMap      | Yes            | `TiledMap`, `TiledMapAsset`, `TiledLayer`, `TiledObjectGroup`, `TiledTile`, `TiledUserNodeData` | tmx XML string, tsx text, sprite frames            | name lookup by parallel arrays       |
| Particle 2D   | Yes            | `ParticleSystem2D`, `ParticleAsset`                                                             | plist text parsed at run time                      | plist key names and blend enum slots |
| Motion streak | Yes            | `MotionStreak`, `MotionStreakAssemblerManager`                                                  | a plain `Texture2D`                                | no `MotionStreak2D` exists           |
| Billboard     | Yes            | `Billboard`                                                                                     | any `Texture2D` the app keeps alive                | `width` and `height` default to 0    |

## Contracts

Create the Canvas component before assigning its camera. Use runtime payloads, not Creator imports. Spine remains backend/asset blocked; particle plist fields and blend factors follow the native runtime contract.

# Cocos AIR agent session and inspection

Use the [environment rules](references/context.md) to locate the checkout or installed package; sibling skills are optional direct dependencies, not a recursive load list.

Drive and observe a running Cocos AIR app through two distinct faces: the runtime face (the `window.__airApp` binding the app sets itself plus the bounded `AirDiagnostics` channel on the main entry) and the devtools face (the `tools/debug/**` session protocol, scene/node snapshots, frame capture, error ring buffer, and pixel probes). The devtools face is NOT part of the default runtime bundle and is not importable from `cocosair`; keep it out of shipped app code.

## Quick Start

Read [references/quick-start.md](references/quick-start.md) when constructing the minimal example. It preserves the complete setup and teardown sequence; select the source-checkout or npm-consumer environment first.

## Related skills

Read [references/context.md](references/context.md#related-skills) to select the owner of this step and only its directly needed dependencies. Reuse already loaded skills; this is not a recursive load list.

## When to use what

- "let an agent or panel see the running app" -> the app sets `window.__airApp = app` (`examples/automation/main.ts:31`); the devtools panel reads `options.app ?? window.__airApp` (`tools/debug/panel.ts:67`). There is no runtime global the engine installs for you.
- "read the scene structure" -> `session.inspectScene()` for a flat `SceneSummary`, `session.inspectNode(id)` for a `NodeSummary` (`tools/debug/agent-session.ts:451`, `:505`). Observation is read-only and never adds asset refs.
- "apply a controlled change" -> `session.dispatch({ requestId, action, targetId, params })` for a whitelisted write (`tools/debug/agent-session.ts:665`). Writes require the target to be inside `writableScenes`; otherwise `OUT_OF_SCOPE`.
- "prove a frame changed" -> `session.captureFrame()` reads the canvas on the AFTER_DRAW hook (`tools/debug/agent-session.ts:589`).
- "collect what broke at runtime" -> devtools `session.getRuntimeErrors()` ring buffer (`tools/debug/agent-session.ts:647`) versus the runtime `app.diagnostics` bounded channel (`src/air/diagnostics.ts:14`).
- "measure a rendered region" -> `tools/debug/pixel-regions.mjs` conventions, screenshot top-left origin versus raw canvas bottom-left (`tools/debug/pixel-regions.mjs:5`, `:53`).

## Contracts

Agent sessions are devtools-only and require explicit writable scope. Inspect session-local IDs before writes. Duplicate request IDs are rejected; capture waits for AFTER_DRAW. Runtime diagnostics are a separate API.

Read [references/contracts.md](references/contracts.md) only when the task needs exact option rules, limits, error behavior or source annotations. Prefer the topic references below for a narrower question.

## Common Mistakes

Before implementing the relevant path, read its wrong/right examples in [references/common-mistakes.md](references/common-mistakes.md):

- [HIGH] Blindly retrying a write with the same requestId
- [HIGH] Treating the devtools session as a default-runtime API in app code
- [MEDIUM] Confusing the runtime diagnostics channel with the devtools error ring buffer
- [MEDIUM] Reading raw canvas pixels with a screenshot-style origin

# Cocos AIR animation and tween contracts

Use the [environment rules](references/context.md) to locate the checkout or installed package; sibling skills are optional direct dependencies, not a recursive load list.

Move things over time two ways: the code-first `tween(target)` chain (zero assets, the shortest path) and the native `Animation` component driving an `AnimationClip` you can build entirely in code. Both are stepped by the director, never by your own `requestAnimationFrame`. For deterministic evidence there is a third, test-only driver, `createStepClock`, that pauses the real clock and advances one frame at a time.

## Quick Start

Read [references/quick-start.md](references/quick-start.md) when constructing the minimal example. It preserves the complete setup and teardown sequence; select the source-checkout or npm-consumer environment first.

## Related skills

Read [references/context.md](references/context.md#related-skills) to select the owner of this step and only its directly needed dependencies. Reuse already loaded skills; this is not a recursive load list.

## When to use what

- "move/scale/rotate something over time, no assets" -> `tween(target).to(...).start()`; the chain is a sequence and `repeatForever()` loops the union ([tween-ops.md](references/tween-ops.md)).
- "run two motions at once on one target" -> just start two tweens on the same target; they time independently. `parallel(...)` is only for packing a parallel group into a larger sequence.
- "reusable keyed animation, or a glTF clip" -> `Animation` component + `AnimationClip`; build the clip in code with `animation.VectorTrack` and `animation.TrackPath` ([animation-clip.md](references/animation-clip.md)).
- "loop a clip" -> set `clip.wrapMode = AnimationClip.WrapMode.Loop` before play, or set `state.wrapMode` (which resets time and repeatCount) ([animation-clip.md](references/animation-clip.md)).
- "per-frame game logic" -> `Component.update(dt)` / `lateUpdate(dt)` / `this.schedule(cb, interval)`; multiply by `dt`, never assume a fixed frame rate (`docs/manual/how-to-update-things.md`).
- "deterministic frames for a test or evidence capture" -> `createStepClock()`; `begin()` then `await step(dt)` then `end()`, and never run it while the real pacer is live ([step-clock.md](references/step-clock.md)).
- "state-machine / pose-graph animation" -> not published; `marionette` and `procedural-animation` are out of the default feature set ([animation-clip.md](references/animation-clip.md)).

## Contracts

Use one clock for native updates and deterministic steps. Preserve tween target ownership; pose-graph availability requires checking the actual entry. `WrapMode` is accessed through `AnimationClip.WrapMode`.

Read [references/contracts.md](references/contracts.md) only when the task needs exact option rules, limits, error behavior or source annotations. Prefer the topic references below for a narrower question.

## Common Mistakes

Before implementing the relevant path, read its wrong/right examples in [references/common-mistakes.md](references/common-mistakes.md):

- [HIGH] Importing track classes by name
- [HIGH] Running the real pacer and the step clock at once
- [HIGH] Assuming `reverseTime(embedTween)` returns to the start
- [MEDIUM] Setting `wrapMode` every frame to keep a clip looping
- [MEDIUM] Citing marionette or pose-graph animation as available

Use the [environment rules](references/context.md) to locate the checkout or installed package; sibling skills are optional direct dependencies, not a recursive load list.

Load assets through the Code First registry and the reference-counted bank, build textures from canvas and pixel data, and parse libGDX atlases and BMFont pages - there is no Creator bundle pipeline here, so every bundle-era snippet needs re-grounding.

## Quick Start

Read [references/quick-start.md](references/quick-start.md) when constructing the minimal example. It preserves the complete setup and teardown sequence; select the source-checkout or npm-consumer environment first.

## When to use what

- "load a JSON/manifest file at runtime" -> `loadAssetAsync(url)` with no type argument (`src/air/utils/load-asset.ts:38`, `:68-77`).
- "load something I built in code" -> `assetManager.assets.add(key, asset)` then `loadAssetAsync(key, Type)` (`:60-62`); see `examples/ui-asset-loading/src/main.ts:339-342` for the round-trip shape.
- "load a png/jpg/audio/text by URL" -> `new AssetBank().load(url, { ext })` for refcounted ownership, or `assetManager.loadRemote` when you accept the engine's URL cache ([asset-bank.md](references/asset-bank.md)).
- "load a model" -> not this skill; `loadAssetAsync` routes `.gltf`/`.glb` to `GLTFLoader` (`src/air/utils/load-asset.ts:40-43`), see [cocosair-gltf](references/context.md#related-skills).
- "texture from pixels without a file" -> `new ImageAsset(canvasElement)` plus `texture.image =` (`src/cocos/asset/assets/image-asset.ts:670`, `src/cocos/asset/assets/texture-2d.ts:161-163`); to refill a level from a typed array, `reset(info)` then `uploadData(source, level)` ([texture2d.md](references/texture2d.md)).
- "sprite sheets" -> `parseAtlasText`/`createAtlasHandle` for libGDX text atlases; Creator `.plist` atlases are not this parser's input ([atlas.md](references/atlas.md)).
- "custom font" -> `loadBitmapFont(url, { bank })` then `label.font = handle.font`; the Creator TTF/font-asset workflow does not exist here ([bmfont.md](references/bmfont.md)).
- "the same URL hands back a destroyed asset, or a handle refuses to dispose" -> `assetManager.releaseAsset(asset)` before re-loading and never `destroy()` alone ([asset-bank.md](references/asset-bank.md)); `AIR_E_ATLAS_IN_USE` and `AIR_E_FNT_IN_USE` both mean someone still holds a reference, so detach the component first ([atlas.md](references/atlas.md), [bmfont.md](references/bmfont.md)).
- "how do I know this actually works in a browser" -> the evidence column of each reference names the validator, not just the example id.

## Contracts

AIR has no implicit Creator resources bundle. Keep ImageAsset/Texture2D and cache/refcount ownership distinct; detach users before disposing handles. Abort cancels a subscriber, not the shared underlying request.

# Cocos AIR camera

Use the [environment rules](references/context.md) to locate the checkout or installed package; sibling skills are optional direct dependencies, not a recursive load list.

Frame a scene with the original `Camera` component: choose the projection and its clip planes, decide which layers it draws and in what order, and convert between world space and the physical screen rectangle it renders into. AIR ships no Creator camera preview; every camera is built and configured in code.

## Quick Start

Read [references/quick-start.md](references/quick-start.md) when constructing the minimal example. It preserves the complete setup and teardown sequence; select the source-checkout or npm-consumer environment first.

## When to use what

- "Put a view into a scene" -> `node.addComponent(Camera)`; the render object is `camera.camera` (`src/cocos/misc/camera-component.ts:202`).
- "Switch perspective and orthographic framing" -> `camera.projection`, plus `fov`/`fovAxis` or `orthoHeight`/`orthoWidth`; table in [camera-projection.md](references/camera-projection.md).
- "Fit a loaded model in view" -> `frameObject(camera, target, fallbackDistance?)` (`src/air/utils/frame-object.ts:35`).
- "Split-screen or picture-in-picture" -> `camera.rect` (normalized viewport `Rect`).
- "Two cameras, who draws on top" -> `camera.priority` + `camera.clearFlags`; behavior in [multi-camera.md](references/multi-camera.md).
- "Which nodes does this camera draw" -> `camera.visibility` layer mask (bit values owned by cocosair-scene-graph).
- "Convert a pointer pixel to a world ray / node position" -> `camera.screenToWorld`, `camera.screenPointToRay`, `camera.convertToUINode`; coordinate space in [screen-world.md](references/screen-world.md).
- "Clip at an arbitrary near plane (mirror, water)" -> `camera.camera.calculateObliqueMat(Vec4)` and `camera.camera.getClipSpaceMinz()`.

## Contracts

Use component conversion methods and left-bottom framebuffer pixels. `worldToScreen` and `screenToWorld` use different depth conventions; prefer a ray for picking. Camera visibility must include the node layer.
